abstract: Mitosis is associated with dramatic remodeling of intracellular organelles that supports their equal distribution between daughter cells. Recent investigations into membrane contact sites (MCS) show that they also remodel in mitosis with a significant loss of ER-plasma membrane CS (ERPMCS). However, the mechanisms governing this loss are unknown. Here we show that phosphorylation of the ERPMCS tether extended synaptotagmin 2 (E-Syt2) facilitates the loss of ERPMCS in mitosis. Preventing E-Syt2 phosphorylation in mitosis rescues the loss of ERPMCS. The persistence of ERPMCS is associated with delayed growth and progression through mitosis. This shows that E-Syt2 mitosis specific phosphorylation regulates its tethering potential and that the loss of ERPMCS is important for timely cell division.
